title: ar
goal: Read and spell words with r-controlled **ar** (/ar/, as in car, farm, start) — the first r-controlled vowel, taught here (matching UFLI/RWI sequencing) before any vowel team so common everyday words stop leaking into earlier lessons.
review: VCe (all 5 vowels), drop-e, open syllables, y=/ē//ī/, soft c/g, -ce/-ge/-dge
heartLine: whole, earth (last two of the 16 Level 3 heart words — all Level 3 heart words are now taught)

spell.sentence: The car is in the yard.

listen.passage: Farmers markets let shoppers buy food directly from the people who grew it, which often means the produce is fresher than what has traveled a long distance to a big store. Buying this way also supports the local economy.

tier2.def: the way money and goods move around in a place — who earns it, who spends it, who it helps.
tier2.full: the way money and goods move around in a place — who earns it, who spends it, who it helps.

questions: Why might food from a farmers market be fresher?
What's one small way people can support their local economy?

dictation: Sam and his mom start the car

A.text: Sam and his mom go to the farm. / A big, red barn is at the farm. / Sam pets a cute pup and a fat pig. / "A big cart!" said Sam. / He rides in the cart with his mom, because he likes it a lot. / They spot a hen in the yard. / Once they are done, they have a snack of grapes. / Sam has a whole, fine time at the farm.

B.text: Kate got a job at the market. / She helps at a cart that sells fresh grapes and plums. / At nine, she sets up the cart and starts her shift. / "This job is hard, but I like it," said Kate. / She helps many people at the market, because she likes to help. / Once her shift is done, Kate has a snack and a cup of milk. / She has a whole, fine time at the market.
